idiom_name: Rack middleware stack (use) + Strong Parameters for payload rules
implementation_notes: Rack standardizes the interception layer: a middleware is any object that takes the next application and calls it from `#call(env)`, so `use ValidateIngress` early in the stack validates every request before it reaches Rails, and returning a 400 tuple without calling the inner app is the rejection; the Rack SPEC even fixes what middleware may do with the response body. Model-shaped rules belong to Strong Parameters (`params.expect(person: [:name, :age])` / `permit`), which raises instead of silently mass-assigning unpermitted attributes. Keep Active Model validations for domain/business rules after the controller accepted the data - they are not an ingress layer.
pitfalls: Middleware order matters: a validator needing the session or the authenticated user must be inserted after those middleware, and `use` added after the router never sees the request.
Per the Rack SPEC the returned body must be a fresh object and the original consumed body must be closed; buffering the inner response without closing it leaks resources and breaks streaming.
params.expect/permit! with an empty hash permits arbitrary input - keep the permitted key list explicit, since that check is the layer's payload half.
